page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. The memory configuration provides 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX-512 vector extensions with VNNI support, cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI, and cache resources consisting of 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache.

Unlike diskless D-series variants, the D4ds_v5 includes 161 GB of temporary local SSD storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight moderate single-threaded compute, showing average performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 1639.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1896.58. Multi-core compute falls into the lower quartile, reflecting the 2-core physical limit with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3502.0 and PassMark CPU score of 5958.73. Memory throughput measures 29.78 GB/sec for uncached reads and 25.32 GB/sec for uncached writes, while static web serving throughput reaches 6.57 GB/sec.

The bundled temporary SSD provides low-latency workspace for temporary caching and paging files without requiring additional persistent disk attachments for scratch data. However, the limited physical core count restricts parallel processing capability, as evidenced by low throughput in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and database transaction tests. The instance is suitable for balanced web serving, application middleware, microservices, development environments, and small-scale caching workloads that benefit from integrated local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v5 is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading. The configuration delivers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio alongside 161 GB of attached local SSD scratch storage. Single-threaded performance sits within average benchmark distributions, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1639.0 and steady gzip compression throughput. However, multi-core computational throughput and database transaction operations remain modest due to the two physical core constraint. The integrated local SSD makes this instance cost-effective for workloads requiring fast temporary storage without incurring auxiliary disk overhead. It is appropriately suited for lightweight web application serving, CI/CD pipeline workers, API middleware, and entry-level container deployments.
